The words

The Lord on high proclaims
His Godhead from his throne;
"Mercy and justice are the names
"By which I will be known.

"Ye dying souls that sit
"In darkness and distress,
"Look from the borders of the pit
"To my recovering grace."

Sinners shall hear the sound;
Their thankful tongues shall own,
"Our righteousness and strength is found
"In thee, the Lord, alone."

In thee shall Israel trust,
And see their guilt forgiven;
God will pronounce the sinners just,
And take the saints to heaven.

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum Eb and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on d (E♭), on the word “The”, as a pickup before the first full bar.
  • Count the time. 4/4 means four crotchet beats in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m f s l t. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 85, headed “The same”.

Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to FRANCONIA; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.

  • Words (1707): Isaac Watts (1674–1748)
  • Music (1738): Johann Balthasar König (1691–1758)

Melody from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune FRANCONIA by Johann Balthasar König (1691–1758); words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748). Questions about The Lord on High Proclaims

What is the doh of The Lord on High Proclaims?

In this version, in Eb major, doh is Eb. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does The Lord on High Proclaims start on?

It starts on d (E♭ in Eb major), a pickup on the word “The” before the first full bar. Find doh first, then sing up or down to d.

Is The Lord on High Proclaims in the public domain?

Yes. Isaac Watts died in 1748, Johann Balthasar König died in 1758; the words were first published in 1707 and the music in 1738. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
